llm.role: designed the plane census and the lift, wrote the runner and the certificate

notes: Every stabilizer decomposition of |sqrtT>^m has a span containing the four-dimensional Galois-forced subspace V4 (cert_sqrtt_galois.py), and chi(|sqrtT>^5) = 6 exactly (qubit_sqrtT-m5-lower-6.json). Six terms at m = 5 are therefore independent with residues modulo V4 spanning a plane, and pivoting on one term reduces the census to residue classes modulo V4 + span(pivot), computed exactly modulo two primes with every candidate class re-decided over Q(zeta_16). Over all 8,585 orbit representatives under the qubit permutations and the diagonal Clifford S^(x)5 (which maps the set of decompositions to itself through the Galois automorphism zeta -> zeta^13), the only candidate set is the 18 permutation-symmetric five-qubit stabilizer states, so every six-term decomposition of |sqrtT>^5 lies inside Sym^5: exactly 3,375 of them, 852 orbits. Both computational slices of |sqrtT>^6 are |sqrtT>^5 up to the scalar zeta, so a six-term decomposition of |sqrtT>^6 would slice to two six-term decompositions of |sqrtT>^5 related term by term by a Pauli and a fourth root of unity; the lift searches every pair in the complete list and finds none. Hence chi(|sqrtT>^6) >= 7, and the cell is 7 <= chi <= 12 (qubit_sqrtT-m6-upper-12.json). The enumeration was not re-run under the budget: it is attested by the stored block outputs and the committed runner; the certificate re-runs two blocks from a printed seed, checks the orbit coverage of the stored pivots, and runs the exact collection and the lift in full. chi <= 7 at this cell would beat the published exponent 1/2.
